title: Monolith Retail - Credits to Live & Hosting Fit (discovery)
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private fit
summary: Initial discovery focused on Monolith's timeline to ship assistant features. They prefer a PLG path to validate with free credits and measure time-to-first-token. Key concerns: data residency, SOC2, KMS integration, and predictable latency for peaks. AE/SE outlined hosted quickstart, Dedicated reserved capacity, and private VPC options; SE proposed a lightweight pilot using hosted credits + a dedicated benchmarking run.
action_items: Maya Chen: Send security pack (SOC2, ISO) and KMS integration notes by 2028-06-03
Rafael Ortega: Provision benchmark script and shared prompt set, run initial latency test vs their sample payloads by 2028-06-07
Evan Grant: Create Redwood org and invite AE/SE to the account by 2028-06-04
next_steps: Send pricing sheet and dedicated capacity tiers
Share quickstart guide + one-click credit redemption link
Schedule 1-hour technical bench on 2028-06-08 to run peak throughput test
meeting_header:
Date: 2028-06-01 | 15:00-15:46 UTC | Duration: 46m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rafael Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Das (Redwood Solutions), Evan Grant (Monolith Head of Product), Sana Iqbal (ML Eng Lead), Tom Reid (Infra)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everybody, thanks for taking the time. quick around the room?
[00:08] Evan Grant: Hi Evan here, head of product at Monolith — we run catalog search, personalization and a small assistant team.
[00:12] Sana Iqbal: Sana - ML eng lead, focused on inference cost and latency.
[00:16] Tom Reid: Tom - infra, network and compliance touchpoints.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Great. Rafael from SE will go deeper on performance later. High level, we want to understand time-to-first-token for your team, get you live with minimal friction, and cover hosting options — hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, or Private VPC.
[00:35] Rafael Ortega: hi, Rafael. quick thing — is Monolith planning to kick off with a small PLG trial or go straight to a pilot with dedicated capacity?
[00:42] Evan Grant: We're leaning PLG first. want our product folks to play with actual calls. free credits would help. timeline is 4–6 weeks to a public small feature.
[00:51] Maya Chen: Perfect, that's our usual path. we'll give credits and a quickstart playbook so you can hit TTFT — time-to-first-token — in hours.
[01:02] Sana Iqbal: Important for us: predictable latency under 95th percentile, and data residency for PII-ish product logs. Also SSO and audit logs.
[01:11] Tom Reid: Also KMS for customer keys and we need SOC2 evidence. any on-prem option?
[01:16] Maya Chen: Yes. short answers: hosted API is fastest for TTFT and PLG; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput; Private gives you the VPC/on-prem control you may need for data residency. We'll send SOC2 and KMS docs after.
[01:29] Rafael Ortega: To make this concrete — for PLG quickstart we recommend: 1) create an org, 2) redeem free credits, 3) run our sample load test and 4) share prompts and a small evaluation set. That shows cost/latency per route.
[01:45] Sana Iqbal: Can you outline expected latency numbers for hosted vs dedicated for a 2k token request?
[01:50] Rafael Ortega: ballpark: hosted with our optimized open models — a 2k token generation is ~300–500ms per token for initial warm steps, end-to-end might be 800–1200ms for typical models; dedicated on a pinned GPU fleet can reduce tail to ~400–700ms because of reserved capacity and less noisy neighbors. numbers vary with quantization and seq length.
[02:14] Evan Grant: that's helpful. what about cost delta?
[02:17] Maya Chen: Hosted is usage-based, good for early PLG. Dedicated is higher committed cost but reduces per-token unit price at scale. Redwood Optimize also recommends batching/quantization profiles to lower cost.
[02:28] Tom Reid: For private, we need to know networking: can we keep data inside our cloud region and integrate with our KMS?
[02:33] Rafael Ortega: yep — Private supports customer-managed networking and KMS/HSM integrations. small caveat: on-prem air-gapped is more involved and has a longer lead time.
[02:45] Sana Iqbal: transcription note — sometimes these things say KV cache but it comes out as KV cash in notes, not a blocker.
[02:50] Maya Chen: true — lol.
[02:52] Evan Grant: ok, about TTFT — we have a platform engineer who wants to try to hit a demo with engineers in 48 hours. is that realistic?
[02:59] Rafael Ortega: Yes. If you accept hosted credits and we pre-provision a sandbox org, typical TTFT is under 24 hours for basic integration: API key, SDK, run simple summarize/qa calls. the only friction is SSO and private network setups which add days.
[03:14] Tom Reid: SSO is important — we use Okta and need SAML.
[03:18] Maya Chen: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user sync, we can include docs.
[03:24] Sana Iqbal: For security review — do you retain logs? we need to ensure product logs with user PII are not stored unless encrypted.
[03:31] Rafael Ortega: We have configurable log retention and can provide audit logs; for Private/Dedicated you can opt for no-logs retention or self-managed logging. we'll share the exact retention options in the security pack.
[03:45] Evan Grant: Great. ok, let's talk about a simple pilot. we want to run a small assistant with 100k tokens/month initially and measure latency under load. how do we set that up?
[03:56] Maya Chen: Steps: redeem PLG credits, integrate SDK, run our benchmark script over your sample queries, then choose whether you want to convert to Dedicated reserve if throughput needs support. Rafael — can you sketch the benchmark?
[04:08] Rafael Ortega: Sure. We'll provide a load harness that does token-level tracing, measures 50/90/95/99th latencies, and reports per-model costs. We'll also include a KV/prefix cache test to show cost delta. plan is: baseline on hosted, then optionally run same harness on a Dedicated slot with reserved GPUs to compare.
[04:28] Sana Iqbal: Are your default models open weights or proprietary? we've seen drift in hallucination and want model verifiability.
[04:36] Rafael Ortega: We curate open models and also offer Redwood-verified performance profiles; you can pin model versions for rollouts. for higher quality we recommend a larger variant, but redeploying to Dedicated is straightforward.
[04:48] Tom Reid: Any compliance red flags for us if we start on hosted? cause we're regulated in EU and want data residency in eu-west-1.
[04:56] Maya Chen: Hosted can be regionally isolated — we have EU regions; for strict residency Private deployment is the safest. We'll flag that in the security doc.
[05:05] Evan Grant: Good. Can you give an example of 'time-to-first-token' path we can give to our engs? like step-by-step?
[05:11] Maya Chen: Yes — 1) sign up and create org, 2) redeem credit link we send, 3) create API key, 4) follow quickstart with our SDK (node/python snippet), 5) run sample prompt set and the benchmark script. with hosted you'll see first tokens in ~15 minutes after SDK setup; full TTFT for a small feature demo usually under a day.
[05:29] Rafael Ortega: I'll paste code in the thread after this call. sample: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"summarize..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate (note: transcription might mangle slashes).
[05:42] Sana Iqbal: For benchmarks, will your harness simulate KV cache hits? our workloads are very cache-heavy.
[05:48] Rafael Ortega: yes, it includes a prefix/KV cache pattern. we can also show savings with continuous batching.
[05:55] Evan Grant: Anything else we should consider around costs?
[05:58] Maya Chen: Consider quantization — Redwood Optimize can recommend quant & batching to cut cost 30–60% depending on latency constraints. also route policy: route cheap requests to smaller models to save money.
[06:12] Tom Reid: when would Dedicated make sense?
[06:15] Rafael Ortega: if you have steady high throughput and must hit tail latency SLOs. also if you need capacity isolation. for early PLG, hosted is typically better.
[06:25] Evan Grant: ok. here's a small wrinkle — legal wants to see a procurement timeline and a demo to show execs. can we script a 10–15 minute exec demo with metrics?
[06:34] Maya Chen: yes, we can prepare a short demo that shows latency, cost per token, and a live assistant scenario. we'll need sample prompts and expected success criteria.
[06:44] Sana Iqbal: success criteria: 95th < 1.2s for typical assistant queries, and token cost < $0.0008/token (ballpark).
[06:52] Rafael Ortega: we'll use those numbers for the bench. quick note: token pricing depends on model size; we can run a cost estimate spreadsheet.
[07:01] Evan Grant: Are there any quick blockers for the 48-hour TTFT push?
[07:05] Rafael Ortega: only SSO/KMS/private network. if you skip SSO and use API keys and hosted credits, we can get you first tokens same day.
[07:14] Tom Reid: ok, we'll do hosted credits first. legal will still want the SOC2 docs and a short data processing addendum.
[07:22] Maya Chen: we'll include DPA and SOC2 in the security pack.
[07:26] Evan Grant: on the credits — how are they redeemed?
[07:29] Maya Chen: we'll send a single-use redemption link tied to the org you create. clicking it adds the credit to billing account and unlocks more API quotas for trial.
[07:37] Sana Iqbal: can credits be split across teams?
[07:39] Maya Chen: yes, you can allocate routes and API keys per project, and track spending per token in the console.
[07:45] Rafael Ortega: also, console gives token-level cost breakdowns per route and model which helps governance.
[07:52] Evan Grant: ok let's get concrete on dates. we'll create the org tomorrow, invite you, and you provide security pack and bench.
[07:58] Maya Chen: noted. i'll send security pack by monday. Rafael will share bench harness and prompt set.
[08:04] Tom Reid: can you attach a short runbook for switching to Dedicated if the pilot shows we need it?
[08:09] Rafael Ortega: yes — there is a simple migration path: pin model version, configure autoscale policies, transfer to reserved capacity. we'll include the runbook.
[08:19] Evan Grant: are there any performance gotchas with quantized models?
[08:22] Rafael Ortega: quantization helps cost but sometimes impacts quality on some prompt patterns; we'll include A/B eval guidance. Redwood Optimize flags regressions on prompt sets.
[08:33] Maya Chen: Alright, last thing — sharing artifacts. we'll drop three links: quickstart, credit redemption, and security pack. any other asks?
[08:42] Sana Iqbal: ask Rafael to include an example of 2k token request results and the per-token breakdown.
[08:47] Rafael Ortega: will do.
[08:49] Evan Grant: cool, recap: create org and invite, Redwood sends credits + security docs, Rafael provides bench, schedule 1-hour bench session next week.
[08:59] Maya Chen: exactly. i'll follow up with calendar invites. thanks everyone.
[09:03] (call ends)

Notes: occasional transcription glitches (SAML sometimes shows as S A M L, KV cache as KV cash). Links referenced during call: Quickstart guide (link), Credit redemption (link), Security pack (link).
